chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ribʿī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who sells the fruit and then excludes a measured amount and dates, he said: “There is no harm in it.”

He said: And a servant of his was sitting with him, so the servant said: “He indeed sells and excludes awsāq,” meaning Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. He said: So he looked at him and did not disapprove of that statement of his.

key_terms.أَوْسَاقًا: large measured quantities used in trade
key_terms.الثَّمَرَةَ: the fruit being sold in the transaction
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.يَسْتَثْنِي: to exclude or reserve a portion from the sale

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islamic law to sell fruit while excluding a specified measured amount from the sale?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a commercial ruling about selling fruit while excluding a specified measured portion from the sale. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام permits this transaction, and the report further indicates this was a known and accepted practice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3788 - Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Ribi, who reported from Abu Abdillah (as):

Regarding a man who sells fruits and then excludes a specific measure (a portion) of dates,
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it."

It was mentioned that one of his servants was sitting with him, and the servant said:
"He indeed sells and excludes certain measures (Awsaq)" - referring to Abu Abdillah (as).
Imam (as) then looked at him and did not disapprove of what he had said.
